strings: The Moonshrine Ruins are a flooded expanse of ancient night elven architecture deep within Blackfathom Deeps. Once dedicated to the worship of Elune, these crumbling halls have been desecrated and seized by the Twilight's Hammer cult.

Past the cavernous Pool of Ask'ar lies the Moonshrine Ruins, a somber testament to the night elves' ancient past along the Ashenvale coast. These partially submerged halls once rang with chants honoring the Moon Goddess Elune, but the Great Sundering shattered the temple and drowned its lower levels in sea water. Today, the murky waters churn with feral aquatic beasts, from aggressive crabs to serpentine threshadons, while the Twilight's Hammer cult maintains an active presence throughout the stones, bent on dark rituals that mock the shrine's sacred origin.

Connecting directly toward the Forgotten Pool and the Moonshrine Sanctum, the ruins serve as a staging ground for the cult's summonings. Beneath the surface of the flooded chambers sits an ancient runestone bound to the elements. Through this aquatic focus, the Twilight's Hammer manipulates the waters of the deeps, calling forth Baron Aquanis, a monstrous water elemental bound to their dark designs.
What were the Moonshrine Ruins originally built for?
The ruins were originally part of a grand underground temple complex dedicated to the night elven goddess Elune, constructed before the Great Sundering tore the ancient continent apart.

Moonshrine Sanctum is an ancient elven shrine deep within Blackfathom Deeps, now serving as the inner redoubt for the Twilight's Hammer cult. Presided over by Twilight Lord Kelris, the chamber houses a pristine monument to Queen Azshara and directly guards the sealed entrance to Aku'mai's lair.

Situated just beyond the flooded Moonshrine Ruins, the Moonshrine Sanctum represents the central hub of cultist activity inside Blackfathom Deeps. Though originally built millennia ago by night elves to honor the moon and their rulers, the hall is now defiled by the Twilight's Hammer. Interestingly, the cultists have carefully maintained the towering effigy of Queen Azshara, finding kinship with the serpentine naga who serve the same dark, submerged masters. Under the watchful gaze of Twilight Lord Kelris, dark rituals are chanted day and night beneath the cavernous stone ceiling.

The sanctum acts as the final barricade before Aku'mai's Lair. Heavy double stone doors seal away the monstrous hydra, held fast by ancient warding enchantments. Surrounding Azshara's central statue are four ritual braziers that must be ignited to unravel the seal. Doing so disturbs the slumbering guardians of the shrine—hordes of giant crabs, snapped-jaw turtles, armored makrura, and conjured water elementals bound to defend the sanctum against unwary intruders.

The Moonshrine Sanctum is located deep inside the Blackfathom Deeps dungeon along the Zoram Strand in Ashenvale. It lies just past the flooded Moonshrine Ruins, immediately preceding the lair of the hydra Aku'mai.

The Moonspray is an Alliance transport vessel belonging to the Kaldorei Fleet. It provides essential maritime passage across the waters separating mainland Kalimdor from the great World Tree, Teldrassil.

The Moonspray serves as an indispensable lifeline between the docks of Auberdine on Darkshore's coast and Rut'theran Village at the root of Teldrassil. Traversing the Veiled Sea, the transport carries adventurers, couriers, and vital provisions between the isolated night elf sanctuary in the crown of the World Tree and the ancient mainland of Kalimdor.
The Moonspray sails between the harbor town of Auberdine in Darkshore and Rut'theran Village, which sits at the oceanic base of Teldrassil.

This secluded shrine, known to the night elves as the Moonwell of Purity, rests in central Ashenvale east of Iris Lake and west of Raynewood Retreat. Its blessed waters channel the grace of Elune to nourish the ancient forest and cleanse creeping foulness from the land. Alliance travelers and night elf sentinels often seek out its tranquil basin to purify corrupted artifacts found in the woodland.

Tucked away beneath the canopy of central Ashenvale, this moonwell serves as a spiritual anchor for the kaldorei. Its luminescent waters tap into nature's latent magic and the light of the Moon Goddess. As the surrounding forest suffers from satyr corruption, fel taint, and logging incursions, pure shrines like this one become vital lifelines for those trying to heal the woods.

The basin acts as the cleansing font in efforts to restore contaminated relics. Adventurers aiding Raene Wolfrunner come here to immerse defiled rod fragments, using the untouched lunar energies to banish corruption where ordinary remedies fail.

This site is known as the Moonwell of Purity. It is one of several moonwells across Ashenvale, located east of Iris Lake and west of Raynewood Retreat.

The Mor'shan Rampart is a heavily fortified Horde barricade positioned at the northern border of the Barrens, guarding the entrance to Ashenvale. Constructed primarily by the Warsong clan, it shields Horde territory from night elf counterattacks while serving as a staging ground for incursions deeper into the forest.

Standing at the northern terminus of the Gold Road, the Mor'shan Rampart marks the transition between the arid plains of the Barrens and the ancient canopies of Ashenvale. Built from heavy timber, defensive palisades, and fortified watchtowers, this bulwark was raised to stem the retaliatory strikes of night elven forces outraged by the Horde's logging operations. It acts both as a shield securing the northern gate to Kalimdor's interior and as a forward staging post for raiding parties pushing north toward Astranaar.

Manned primarily by battle-hardened fighters affiliated with the Warsong clan, the rampart remains under constant military readiness. From these parapets, sentries monitor the tree line for night elf scouts and archers, keeping open supply lines between the frontline outposts of Ashenvale and the greater Horde settlements to the south.

It is a fortified Horde border post situated where the Barrens meets Ashenvale. It was constructed to block Alliance counterattacks from entering the Barrens and to guard the northern end of the Gold Road.

Morgan's Plot is a desolate burial ground and crumbling chapel tucked away just behind the tower of Karazhan in Deadwind Pass. Dominated by restless undead and brooding silence, it holds the forgotten crypts and final resting places of those once tied to Medivh's domain.
A Grave in the Shadow of the Tower

Nestled against the sheer rocky slopes directly behind Karazhan, Morgan's Plot is a sorrowful, overgrown cemetery centered on a ruined chapel and underground crypts. Long before the land decayed into Deadwind Pass, the estate served the burial needs of the tower's inhabitants and nearby grounds. Following the downfall of the Last Guardian, Medivh, dark energies seeped into the earth, driving away all normalcy. Today, restless unliving wander the chapel grounds, haunting the headstones of servants and historic figures alike.
Resting Place of Guardians and Servants

Beneath the crooked tombstones and inside the subterranean catacombs lie the remains of several figures tied intimately to Karazhan's history. Medivh, his seneschal Moroes, and the tower's cook were laid to rest here following the tragedy that shattered the tower. While mysteries linger as to what truly remains in the crypts beneath the soil, the soil itself feels heavy with old, lingering arcana and unquiet spirits.
Morgan's Plot lies in southern Deadwind Pass, situated in a gloomy hollow directly behind the high spire of Karazhan.

Morgan's Vigil is a ruined Alliance redoubt nestled in the southeastern heights of the Burning Steppes. Once a small village, its charred homes and shattered wizard's tower now serve as an austere forward camp for scouts watching the passes to Blackrock Mountain. It remains the sole Alliance foothold in an ash-choked land dominated by Dark Iron dwarves and Blackrock orcs.
The Last Hearth in the Steppes

Perched upon high stone overlooking the fiery wastes, Morgan's Vigil was once a modest settlement before the horrors of the Burning Steppes overran it. Today, charred timbers and the cracked shell of a ruined mage tower stand as grim reminders of the onslaught. The remaining defenders make do beneath rough canvas tents pitched amid the soot. Despite the ruin, the camp retains a gryphon roost, offering an unbroken aerial link back across the mountains to Stormwind City. It serves as a desperately needed haven where scouts, marshals, and passing adventurers catch their breath away from the marauding warbands below.

The outpost draws its name and purpose from the vigilance kept against the looming threat of Blackrock Mountain. With the Dark Iron clan delving deep into dark sorceries and the Blackrock orcs claiming the surrounding wastes, the camp acts as a forward staging ground. Its defenders maintain the camp's defenses, coordinate scouting runs across the ash, and secure the vital pass leading south into Redridge.

The village's houses and other structures were burned to the ground, and its mage tower was left crumbled and destroyed. The surviving inhabitants live in tents among the ruins. The force responsible for the destruction is not identified.

Morlos'Aran is an ancient night elf ruin nestled in the southern reaches of Felwood. Once a proud and thriving settlement before the Great Sundering, it now stands as a grim monument to a lost golden age, drowned under the demonic blight that plagues the surrounding forest.

Ten thousand years ago, prior to the Sundering, Morlos'Aran was a grand urban center of the ancient kaldorei civilization. Much like sister settlements such as Ameth'Aran, Bashal'Aran, and Ordil'Aran across northern Kalimdor, its marble arches and moonlit plazas bustled with elven life and arcana. When the Well of Eternity collapsed, the city broke, leaving only shattered colonnades behind as monuments to their civilization's zenith.

While neighboring ruins in Darkshore and Ashenvale fell to decay and wilderness, Morlos'Aran met a far grimmer fate during the Third War. Positioned directly within the corridor trampled by the Burning Legion, its surviving foundations were choked by demonic corruption and toxic mire. Today, the ruins are haunted by wandering beasts, corrupted elementals, and remnants of the shadow forces lingering in Felwood.

It was a major night elf settlement that thrived before the Great Sundering. Along with sister cities across ancient Kalimdor, it formed part of the core civilization of the kaldorei golden age before falling into ruin ten thousand years ago.

Mortwake's Tower, commonly known as Klaven's Tower or simply the Defias Tower, is a fortified watchtower standing near the river in southeastern Westfall. Commanded by the rogue Klaven Mortwake, it serves as a critical waypoint for smuggling stolen goods across kingdom borders.

Perched on the borderlands north of the Dagger Hills, Klaven's Tower is a vital hub for Defias Brotherhood operations in southern Westfall. Together with Jerod's Landing across the river in Elwynn Forest, the site acts as a receiving post and staging ground for contraband plundered from the Redridge Mountains. Its commanding vantage over the waterways allows the Brotherhood to slip supplies past Kingdom patrols, shielding their logistical network from the crown's eyes.

The tower is controlled by Klaven Mortwake, an alchemist and rogue obsessed with lethal concoctions. Mortwake spends his hours brewing exotic troll poisons within the tower's confines, churning thick, noxious fumes that permeate the upper chambers. While deadly to intruders, the vapors also dull the senses of Mortwake's own guards, providing an exploitable blind spot for stealth operatives sent by Stormwind's intelligence service, SI:7, who monitor the structure from nearby hills.

The tower is held by Klaven Mortwake, a Defias rogue who oversees smuggling operations and conducts experiments with volatile poisons. A contingent of Defias sentries and patrollers guards the grounds under his command.

The Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound is a fortified cavern complex in northern Stranglethorn Vale, situated just south of the ruins of Zul'Gurub. It serves as the primary stronghold for the brute Mosh'Ogg tribe in the jungle, dominated by their ruthless ogre mage chieftain, Mai'Zoth. Long before the ogres made it their home, the mound was a sacred site containing a shrine dedicated to the loa Lukou.
A Den of Ogres and Ancient Faith

Carved into the rugged jungle ridges south of Zul'Gurub, the Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound swarms with brutish Mosh'Ogg maulers, shamans, and warmongers. The ogres seized the cavernous network as an ideal redoubt against hostile jungle trolls and prowling beasts. Yet beneath the crudeness of their settlement lies older history: before the Darkspear tribe departed the southern jungles, this cavern served as a sacred hollow holding a shrine to Lukou, the loa of healing and life. With the departure of the trolls, the shrine fell into neglect, allowing the ogres to claim the subterranean labyrinth for themselves.

Deep within the twisting interior of the mound presides Mai'Zoth, the formidable two-headed ogre mage who commands the Mosh'Ogg clan. In his possession is the Mind's Eye, a potent and dangerous arcane relic that enhances his mental and sorcerous grip over his followers. Mai'Zoth's mastery over magic and raw brute force makes entering the deepest reaches of the mound a peril for any traveler braving northern Stranglethorn.

Mosshide Fen is a swampy, treacherous tract in the eastern Wetlands overrun by the Mosshide gnoll tribe. Dotted with primitive encampments, it is one of the most perilous regions for travelers venturing off the main trade roads.

Sprawling across the murky eastern reaches of the Wetlands, Mosshide Fen serves as the primary domain of the aggressive Mosshide gnolls. The swamp here is dense and tangled, dotted with rough lean-tos and bone-strewn camps. Under the vicious command of pack leaders like Gnawbone, the gnolls fiercely guard their muddy claims, readily ambushing and devouring any travelers, scouts, or prospectors foolish enough to wander into their hunting grounds.

The Mystic Ward is the northwestern district of Ironforge, serving as the dwarven capital's quiet sanctuary for spiritual devotion and arcane study. Distinguishable by its cool, pale blue banners and quiet halls, it stands in stark contrast to the clanging anvils of the nearby Great Forge. Its grandest structure, the Hall of Mysteries, gathers priests, paladins, and mages beneath cavernous stone arches.
A Sanctuary of Faith and Sorcery

While dwarves are famed across Azeroth for their prowess at the forge and on the battlefield, the Mystic Ward represents the kingdom's quieter intellectual and spiritual pursuits. Marked by pale blue heraldry, this cavernous quarter connects the bustling Commons to the Forlorn Cavern and the Great Forge. Within its reaches, merchants supply scholars and spellweavers with regalia, scrolls, and alchemical reagents from shops like The Fighting Wizard and Maeva's Mystical Apparel. Dominating the district is the majestic Hall of Mysteries, where the holy disciplines of the Holy Light intersect with the practiced arts of arcane magic, offering guidance to those who wield unseen powers in defense of the Alliance.

Mystral Lake is the largest body of water in Ashenvale, resting in the south-central forest just below Silverwind Refuge. Once a tranquil sanctuary guarded by water elementals loyal to the night elves, its waters have become fraught with danger due to corruption of the local elementals.

Spanning a vast expanse south of Silverwind Refuge and east of Talondeep Vale, Mystral Lake was long cherished by the kaldorei for its pure waters and peaceful guardian elementals. However, dark interference has broken that ancient peace. The rogue mage Sarilus Foulborne turned his arts upon the lake's water spirits, corrupting them into hostile, violent entities. Today, travelers from both the Horde and Alliance frequently find their journeys pulling them to these troubled shores, contending with the wrath of spirits that once sheltered the woods.

Beyond the corruption troubling the local night elves, Mystral Lake draws attention across faction lines. Horde shaman traveling the path of elemental communion seek out its deep waters during their trials to understand the element of water. Despite the corruption infesting its guardian spirits, the raw primal resonance of the lake makes it an essential pilgrimage site for those learning to bind and respect the tidal spirits.
Mystral Lake lies in south-central Ashenvale. It sits directly south of Silverwind Refuge and east of Talondeep Vale, making it the largest open body of water in the forest.

While the surrounding lands have fallen to banditry and ravenous beasts, the encampment maintains a fragile perimeter where travelers, beleaguered farmers, and recruits can regroup under the watchful eyes of veteran defenders.
